Previous Note: For Hawaii, (1- Incomplete Immunization) was used as a substitute for 2-dose MMR rates - as this is what is provided by the State of Hawaii. Incomplete immunizations includes religious exemptions, medical exemptions, and students with no immunization record or missing immunizations.  The source data is collected by the Department of Health using a random sample of public, private, and charter schools. For this study, school level data was aggregated to county-level using enrollment data.

Vaccination data from Iowa counties includes the number of certificates of immunization provided per county, along with the total enrollment of students per county. The county-level vaccination coverage for Iowa is calculated as follows: [Number of Certificates of Immunization for a County] / [County Total Enrollment].

Children with exemptions based on religious or other grounds may have been vaccinated or were on track to receive vaccinations yet elected not to share their vaccination status with the school. Thus, assessing coverage based on the School Immunization Report alone should be done with caution. Read Idaho Statute 39-4801 for more information: Idaho Statute, Section 39-4801.

Data was aggregated from school-level to county-level using a weighted average [Summation for each school in a county: (School Enrollment Rate * School 2-dose MMR rate)] / [total county enrollment] derived from the  school-level MMR rates and enrollment information provided in the dataset.

Maine provides annual school-level MMR rate data, enrollment data, and the county-level MMR rate data in a centralized database. The aggregated county-level data was utilized for 2018-19 to 2024-25. However, in 2017-18, Maine did not provide the county-level total MMR rate. Therefore, for 2017-18 data the school-level data was aggregated up to county-level using the provided enrollment data and 2-dose MMR data for Kindergarteners.

Data was aggregated from the school building level to the county-level using the enrollment data provided alongside immunization compliance data. Schools with less than 5 students are not included in the report. School data includes both public and private schools. Michigan reported the data for the calendar year, which we aligned with the upcoming school year (i.e., 2023 data was assigned to 2023-24). The 2018-19 data was obtained from Gardner et al., 2020, which used the same methodology for aggregation to county level.

Enrollment data was compiled across public and non-public enrollment available at https://www.nysed.gov/information-reporting-services/student-enrollment-data. BEDS Day enrollment was utilized to match school enrollment to corresponding school ID in the immunization data. County-level rates were calculated across immunization data file using school-level enrollment data and the corresponding MMR rate. Schools where a match between MMR rate database and school-level enrollment data was not found were dropped from the compilation. For the most recent school year (2024-25), 7.4% of schools were not matched, excluding schools that did not provide MMR rates for the most recent school year.
Please note the following:
•	   This data does not include New York City public schools.
•	   For each BEDS enrollment file, the calendar year was matched to the latter school year (i.e., 2018 was matched to 2017-18, 2019 to 2018-19, etc.) as per the documentation.
•	   If a school was duplicated for a given school year and thus had more than one “Percent Immunized Measles” options, the lower bound was used to ensure a more conservative estimate.
•	   The 2021-22 MMR rate for Seneca county does not include Waterloo Highschool, as the MMR rate documented for Waterloo Highschool 9-12 in 2021-22 was 25%, which contrasts with school years 2017-18 to 2024-25 where the MMR rate was higher than 99.80%. Enrollment was consistent during this time period. Due to Waterloo Highschool’s large enrollment, its inclusion drops the 2021-22 Seneca county MMR rate to 89.64%, a delta of ~10% from 2020-21 rates (98.65%) and 2022-23 rates (98.72%). Further, Waterloo Highschool enrollment is only for grades 9-12, who would have been vaccinated pre-pandemic and thus would not experience pandemic-related disruptions in MMR vaccination. Therefore, Waterloo Highschool was excluded from the Seneca county MMR rate due to this improbable outlier in reported MMR rate.

Optional survey for Oklahoma schools. Both public and private schools submitted data; however, the participation rate varies. This data accounts for the following percent of Kindergarten students in the following years. 2019-20: 88% of Kindergarteners in public schools, 53% of private schools; 2020-21: 91% of Kindergarteners in public schools, 61% of private schools; 2021-22: 86% of Kindergarteners in public schools, 46% in private schools; 2022-23: 91% of Kindergarteners in public schools, 65% in private schools; 2023-24: 95% of Kindergarteners in public schools, 62% in private schools; 2024-25:  88% of Kindergarteners in public schools, 66% in private schools.

Oregon Health Authority presents the MMR rates for Sherman and Wasco county as a single combined rate because both of these counties fall under the North Central Public Health District, which is a two-county public health district. We assigned the combined North Central MMR rate to both Wasco and Sherman county.
Additionally, Oregon data was presented as calendar year and assigned to the previous school year based on the observed naming convention of the most recent school year (i.e., 2025 corresponds to 2024-25, 2024: 2023-24, 2023: 2022-23).
Every school in the state self-reports comprehensive immunization data (public, private, and home schooled).

Kindergarten Immunization rates at the city level were mapped to counties, and weighted by city population in 2020 from: https://planning.ri.gov/sites/g/files/xkgbur826/files/documents/census/2021/POP-BY-C%26T-2010---2020.pdf. West Greenwich and West Kingston are not included due to missing data. New Shoreham (2023-24) data is missing and adopts 2022-23 data. Warren (2020-21) data is missing and adopts 2021-22 data. City/Towns are only present if they report more than 10 students.

Complete MMR percent is reported at a county level (both public and private schools) for 2020-21 onwards. For 2019-20 data, the county-level public and private school data was separated. Therefore, we combined public and private school data by weighting public and private county-level data by enrollment data and then aggregating up to county level.
Missing values indicate that the few schools in this county either did not respond to the survey or did not have a Kindergarten class that year.

Counties with <100 kindergartners have been censored in accordance with Utah DHHS data suppression guidelines. Students attending online school have been removed from the county-level totals.  While the physical location of an online school may be in a specific county, that school may draw students residing anywhere in the state.

Missing values indicate that no schools in that county have reported for the selected year. Virginia added HepA to their vaccination requirements in SY 2021, switching from a 4-4-2-3-2 series (4 DTaP, 4 Polio, 2 MMR, 3 HepB, 2 VAR) to a 4-4-2-2-3-2 series at school entry (4DTaP, 4 Polio, 2 MMR, 2 HepA, 3 HepB, and 2 VAR). We included the data due to its completeness; however, we acknowledge that this could contribute to decreases in rates post SY-2021. Please see the following link for further details: https://redcap.vdh.virginia.gov/redcap/surveys/?s=KEJKML9FND4KPFR8. Furthermore, for 2024-25 data Virginia provides school-level 2-dose MMR coverage. To keep consistent with previous years, we kept the full series coverage. Please see the immunization dashboard for school-level rates.

Vermont represents any county with a vaccination rate greater than 95% as >95%. Therefore, we cap all vaccination rates at 0.95 for Vermont. The data is reported to the Vermont Department of Health by all public or independent schools.
Schools with less than 10 individuals are not included due to privacy concerns.
Counties with vaccination coverage exceeding 95% are capped and presented as 95%. Schools and kindergartens with <10 students do not have data shown.

Wyoming only provides 2 MMR school survey data for 2022-2023. All other years are obtained from the Wyoming Immunization Registry (WyIR)and not included in our dataset. Furthermore, Wyoming data for other school years is highly variable by age (2018-19 data collects 2 MMR data from 6-year-olds, state average MMR rate is 71%. School years 2019-20, 2020-21, and 2021-22 collect data for 7-year-olds, where the state averages are 72%, 76%, and 76%, respectively). Wyoming reported the data for the calendar year, which we aligned with the upcoming school year (i.e., 2022 data was assigned to 2022-23). Note, the WyIR tends to underestimate true adolescent coverage because actual vaccines administered is often under-reported, as documented here: https://health.wyo.gov/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/WDH-IMM_Immunization-Data-Technical-Notes-Rev..pdf
